rules.statement: A purchaser of property subject to a lease acquires a right to the rents and profits of such property accruing after such purchase without any assignment of the contract of lease.
rules.supporting_quote: It was argued that the sale of the house passed no interest in the contract of lease under which the house was held, and as the purchaser had taken no assignment of the lease he could not sue for the rent stipulated in the lease. But the passage cited in Voet (XIX. 2, 19) seems to be in point. He says that with the dominum of a land the fruits naturally pass, and if there is a tenant on it the rents take the place of the fruits.
